# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Parent: cand_0001 (val 0.675). I read all 13 failing traces in full and checked each one against the golden workbook. I used the golden files only to name the failure class; no answer values are written into the capability.

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | A. Examples already in the file are ignored or only partly reproduced | 547-43, 409-45, 279-23, 1925 | The agent printed only a sample (rows 2-6) or never printed the "desired result" sheet. It hardcoded a list from that sample, or followed the prose form ('(tig)', 'New') when the same column already held the final form ('tig', 'NEW'). | BEHAVIORAL | Phase 1 skeleton prints desired-result sheets. Phase 3 checklist: reproduce ALL examples (items, text form, layout). Rule: lists are read from the sheet. |
| 2 | B. Wrong source column: prose or wrong letter mapping beats header / formula | 188-39, 45896 | Wrote "name" where the target header says Designation. Mapped ZORD!C:C to the 2nd column. Ignored a cached serial in the target that would have shown which column was meant. | BEHAVIORAL | Phase 1 prints row-1 cells with their column letters. A required per-column mapping comment (target header ← source letter/header ← evidence). Serial→date cross-check. |
| 3 | C. Exact text replaced by a paraphrase or "cleaned" | 203-15, 1925, (51680 partly) | Headers copied from the instruction's paraphrase ('Transport Allowance') instead of the data ('Transport Allowances'). Header text `.strip()`ped. | KNOWLEDGE | prompt §2: labels copied from data are the stored string. |
| 4 | D. Untouched cells inside answer_position | 183-8 (error totals row), 57354 (overwrote filled B3/C3) | The verify step printed only the cells the agent wrote. A '#DIV/0!' totals row inside the range was never recomputed. Pre-filled cells the instruction did not ask for were overwritten with no flag raised. | BEHAVIORAL | Phase 2 verify code scans the WHOLE range and prints ERROR LEFT and CHANGED PRE-FILLED. Phase 3 requires quoting the instruction words that justify each change, otherwise restore. |
| 5 | E. Lookup over-match / list alignment | 524-31, 48975 | Invented substring and alnum fuzzy fallbacks, giving 7 false categories. "Copy rows where yes, skipping others" was row-aligned to a key instead of compacted. | KNOWLEDGE | prompt §2: no looser matching than the instruction describes; filter-and-compact means consecutive rows. |
| 6 | F. Pairing direction of a two-list comparison | 45944 | Agent compared in the wrong direction. One task, no generalizable cue. | — | skipped |
| 7 | G. Golden rewrites the worked-example cells | 51680 | Expected output overwrites the hand-filled G3/G5/G6. This contradicts the protected worked-example rule. | — | skipped (except via cluster C) |

## Changes made this iteration (one row per edit — aim for MULTIPLE classes)
| cluster | edit class (lever) | file | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A, B | SKELETON CODE (inspection) | task_template.md Phase 1 | Each sheet now prints its row-1 cells as (letter, value). A sheet whose title contains desired/expected/sample/example/wanted is printed whole (≤60×20). This is evidence only and changes nothing in the output. | Yes. It adds prints only. The title filter excludes "result"/"output" so ordinary target sheets are not dumped. |
| B, A | EXPLICIT CONTRACT (mapping comment) + worked example | task_template.md, after Phase 1 | A one-line-per-column mapping: target header ← source sheet!letter 'header' ← evidence. Formula letters are mapped via the printed letters. A 5-digit number where a date belongs is converted to a date to find its source column. Lists are read from headers or a lookup, never typed in. The example uses neutral names (Staff/Role, Log/End date). | Yes. It replaces a free-form comment the template already asked for. |
| D | SKELETON CODE (verify scan) | task_template.md Phase 2 | After save, scans all of answer_position: prints ERROR LEFT for real Excel error markers and a CHANGED PRE-FILLED list (count + first 15). | Yes. It only prints. |
| D, A | CHECKLIST | task_template.md Phase 3 | Three items: (1) no ERROR LEFT; (2) each CHANGED PRE-FILLED cell needs quoted instruction words, with the legitimate classes listed (column transformation, fix-and-apply, sort/rebuild, delete-shift), otherwise restore; (3) reproduce ALL finished-looking examples — items, text form, layout. I merged the old "reproduces the worked example" bullet into (3), so nothing is restated. | Mostly. Item (2) names the legitimate change classes, so delete/sort/fix-and-apply tasks (290-1, 469-9, 535-20 class) are not pushed to restore. |
| C, E | KNOWLEDGE (policy with why) | prompt.md §2, new block after the fixed-meaning words | "The instruction's prose is a paraphrase; the workbook holds the exact text": (a) copied labels keep the stored string, with no strip or rephrase; (b) an unmatched lookup stays empty, with no fuzzy fallback the instruction does not describe; (c) filter-and-skip into a list means consecutive rows in source order, scanning the full extent. | Bounded. (a) applies only to text copied from data. (b) applies only when the instruction does not describe the looser match. (c) applies only to "copy rows where X … skipping". |

## Verify-the-fix (one line per change: the trace it targets → what now happens on those exact inputs)
- 409-45: the sheet 'desired result' matches "desired", so its 11 rows print in round 1, including a single blank separator between blocks. Phase 3 item (3) "blank separator rows kept or removed as there" then contradicts the agent's delete-all-empty output.
- 547-43: Phase 1 prints Expected row 1 headers. The mapping rule forbids `target_vars = [...]` typed from rows 2-6, so the list comes from Lookup or Emp headers, which include 'performance'. Phase 3 item (3) "reproduce ALL pre-filled rows" covers Expected rows 2-10, which already include performance rows.
- 45896: the `row 1:` print shows ('C','Valid to'), so ZORD!C:C maps to 'Valid to'. The existing cell I2 '46022,…' converts to 2025-12-31, which equals Valid to. The mapping-comment example uses exactly this pattern with neutral names.
- 188-39: the mapping line for target column B has to cite its header 'Designation', and the example line "target header; the prose said 'name'" covers this case.
- 183-8: the verify scan over I3:L7 prints `ERROR LEFT J7 #DIV/0!` (and K7, L7). The Phase 3 bullet says such a cell gets its recomputed value (the weighted average of the totals row).
- 57354: CHANGED PRE-FILLED prints B3 and C3. The instruction asks for "total revenue and total GP", which justifies only D3/E3. The checklist example is the same pattern with neutral names, so B3/C3 are restored.
- 279-23: the was: list shows B17:B26 already in the form 'tig' in the same column. Phase 3 item (3) "same text form (`abc` vs `(abc)`)" flags '(tig)'.
- 1925: existing C14 = 'NEW' and the user formula has "NEW". Item (3) "`NEW` vs `New`" and §2 paraphrase rule (the example names exactly this) point to 'NEW'.
- 203-15: §2 (a) "'Transport Allowance' for a source value 'Transport Allowances'" — headers are copied from the column-H strings.
- 524-31: §2 (b). The agent's rounds 8-16 added substring/alnum fallbacks, which this rule now forbids; the plain prefix rule from the instruction stays.
- 48975: §2 (c). The 'yes' rows go to B11.. consecutively (Text 1-4, 10, 15, 25), scanning all 33 rows rather than aligning to Output column A.
- Template placeholders: checked with a regex plus str.format. The set is exactly {instruction, spreadsheet_path, spreadsheet_content, instruction_type, answer_position, output_path, max_turns} and formats without error.

## Process & features used
- Subagents / worktrees / parallel features used: none. Serial: 13 traces fit in one context, and the instructions discourage Agent/Workflow unless requested.
- Prior iterations read: RUNMAP, prior_iterations/cand_0001 PROCESS + diff, LEDGER, JOURNAL. Lessons: (1) iter1's §2 word list may have caused regressions 188-39/45896/48975/51680/547-43, but the traces show those regressions come from inspection gaps (partial prints, letter mapping, alignment), not from the word list. So I kept the word list and added inspection structure instead of more rules. (2) The sibling run showed prose growth regresses, so most new content here is skeleton code and checklist, and only one bounded §2 block was added (~170 words).
- rejected.jsonl: empty. No refuted approaches to avoid.

## Good things to PRESERVE (do not let a future iteration undo these)
- From iter1: the data_only read copy plus formula write copy, the '=' scrub, the stall breaker, and the print of every non-empty target cell.
- §1 grading contract, §2 worked-example rule, §2 snapshot/next-item/matrix rules: these protect 9111, 52541, 59511, 50971 and others.
- New: the full-range verify scan (ERROR LEFT / CHANGED PRE-FILLED). It is pure evidence and cheap.

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why)
- 45944 (pairing direction of the outside-list comparison): a single task, and I found no cue in the workbook that a general rule could point to. Any rule would be a guess.
- 51680's rewrite of the hand-filled example cells: the golden contradicts the worked-example rule that protects many passing tasks. Only the no-strip part (§2 a) is targeted.
- Reverting iter1's case-insensitive matching rule (possible tension with 1925): the failure in 1925 was the output literal, not the matching, so I left the rule alone.

# DIAGNOSIS.json — machine-readable diagnosis (OPTIONAL but recommended)

In addition to PROCESS.md, you may write a DIAGNOSIS.json file to make your diagnosis machine-readable for the dashboard. This is optional; if absent, the dashboard will parse PROCESS.md tables when present, or show only outcome data.

The schema:
```json
{
  "candidate": "cand_NNNN",
  "headline": "Brief summary of this iteration's strategy",
  "clusters": [
    {"id": "A", "name": "Short cluster name",
     "detail": "Root cause explanation", "tasks": ["task-id", ...],
     "scope": "BOUNDED|WIDESPREAD|SYSTEMIC", "latent": false,
     "tag": "KNOWLEDGE|BEHAVIORAL|CAPABILITY-GAP"}
  ],
  "edits": [
    {"id": "E1", "title": "What this edit does",
     "files": ["prompt.md"], "lever": "CONTRACT|KNOWLEDGE|BEHAVIORAL|...",
     "clusters": ["A"], "blast_radius": "BOUNDED|MODERATE|WIDE",
     "verified": "How you tested it"}
  ],
  "skipped": [{"title": "What was skipped", "reason": "Why"}],
  "techniques": ["technique 1", "technique 2"]
}
```

Validation is advisory only and never blocks an iteration. Warnings are recorded when:
- A task ID in clusters[].tasks is not in the val split
- An edit references a cluster ID that does not exist
- An edit references a file that does not exist in the candidate
